customer_feedback.detected.action: A customer gave product feedback in person. Resolve who they are, connect the feedback to prior signals, and prepare the follow-up the owner promised. Everything external stays a draft until the owner approves it. Use the execute tool (shell) for all file work: keep every artifact under $HOME/world/<event id>/ and finish by running one verifying shell command that exits 0.

workers.name: Context
workers.brief: GBrain (the owner's declarative memory) is readable through the owner's WORLD service at http://host.docker.internal:8787/gbrain, read-only, bearer auth with the GBRAIN_PROXY_TOKEN env var (always write it as "authorization: Bearer $GBRAIN_PROXY_TOKEN", never print or inline the value). Calls: GET /gbrain/person/<person id>?actor=<your name>&event_id=<event id> (person card: relationship, facts, open loops, last seen); POST /gbrain/query with JSON {"q": ..., "actor": "<your name>", "event_id": "<event id>"} (hybrid search, returns slug, title, snippet); GET /gbrain/page/<slug>?actor=<your name>&event_id=<event id> (one page). Use curl -sS -m 20 and save each response as a .json file in your event dir. If a call fails (unreachable, 401, 503), write the status into the file and continue from the world event alone. Resolve who this person and company are. Use the execute tool (shell) for all file work. 1) mkdir -p $HOME/world/<event id> && cd $HOME/world/<event id>. You MUST read GBrain first: curl the person card for <the first id in the event's people that is not stephen> into gbrain-person.json, then POST /gbrain/query for prior feedback and requests from this person and project (q like "<name> <product> feedback") into gbrain-prior.json. 2) Write context.md there with a five line person card from GBrain plus the event: name, role and company, relationship, last topic, what they owe and what we owe; then a 'GBrain:' line listing the slugs you used. 3) Verify with: test -s $HOME/world/<event id>/context.md && grep -qi 'owe' $HOME/world/<event id>/context.md && echo CONTEXT_OK. Report the card to the root.

workers.name: Product
workers.brief: GBrain (the owner's declarative memory) is readable through the owner's WORLD service at http://host.docker.internal:8787/gbrain, read-only, bearer auth with the GBRAIN_PROXY_TOKEN env var (always write it as "authorization: Bearer $GBRAIN_PROXY_TOKEN", never print or inline the value). Calls: GET /gbrain/person/<person id>?actor=<your name>&event_id=<event id> (person card: relationship, facts, open loops, last seen); POST /gbrain/query with JSON {"q": ..., "actor": "<your name>", "event_id": "<event id>"} (hybrid search, returns slug, title, snippet); GET /gbrain/page/<slug>?actor=<your name>&event_id=<event id> (one page). Use curl -sS -m 20 and save each response as a .json file in your event dir. If a call fails (unreachable, 401, 503), write the status into the file and continue from the world event alone. Treat the feedback as a product signal. Use the execute tool (shell) for all file work. 1) mkdir -p $HOME/world/<event id> $HOME/world/signals; append one line (date, customer, product, feature, feedback) to $HOME/world/signals/<product>-<feature>.log and count distinct customers in it. 2) Query GBrain for similar past feedback on this product and feature (q like "<product> <feature> feedback") into gbrain-similar.json, and for existing procedures (q like "procedures <product> <feature>") into gbrain-procedures.json; read at most two hit pages. 3) Write issue.md in $HOME/world/<event id>/ with: title, evidence with customer count and the GBrain slugs of similar feedback, likely failing stage, suggested fix, and any existing procedure (procedures/...) that applies. Do not file it anywhere. 4) Verify with: test -s $HOME/world/<event id>/issue.md && grep -qi 'evidence' $HOME/world/<event id>/issue.md && echo ISSUE_OK. Report the draft issue to the root.

workers.name: Follow-up
workers.brief: GBrain (the owner's declarative memory) is readable through the owner's WORLD service at http://host.docker.internal:8787/gbrain, read-only, bearer auth with the GBRAIN_PROXY_TOKEN env var (always write it as "authorization: Bearer $GBRAIN_PROXY_TOKEN", never print or inline the value). Calls: GET /gbrain/person/<person id>?actor=<your name>&event_id=<event id> (person card: relationship, facts, open loops, last seen); POST /gbrain/query with JSON {"q": ..., "actor": "<your name>", "event_id": "<event id>"} (hybrid search, returns slug, title, snippet); GET /gbrain/page/<slug>?actor=<your name>&event_id=<event id> (one page). Use curl -sS -m 20 and save each response as a .json file in your event dir. If a call fails (unreachable, 401, 503), write the status into the file and continue from the world event alone. Find what was promised to this person (a commitment in the event, its gbrain_context, or the you_owe_all list from GET /gbrain/person/<person id>?actor=Follow-up) and draft a short reply in the owner's voice that delivers it. Use the execute tool (shell) for all file work. 1) mkdir -p $HOME/world/<event id> and write reply.md there with a To line, the reply body, and a final line STATUS: AWAITING OWNER APPROVAL. Never send email, Slack, or any external message. 2) Verify with: test -s $HOME/world/<event id>/reply.md && grep -q 'AWAITING OWNER APPROVAL' $HOME/world/<event id>/reply.md && echo REPLY_OK. Report the draft to the root.

feature_request.detected.action: A customer asked for a feature in person. Resolve who is asking, spec the change, and dispatch the coding job to the owner's own WORLD builder (host.docker.internal:8787 is the owner's internal service; it runs Claude Code on the owner's laptop against the owner's repo and opens a PR that is never merged; dispatching is pre-approved and sends nothing to the customer). Use the execute tool (shell) for all file work: keep every artifact under $HOME/world/<event id>/ and finish by running one verifying shell command that exits 0.

workers.name: Context
workers.brief: GBrain (the owner's declarative memory) is readable through the owner's WORLD service at http://host.docker.internal:8787/gbrain, read-only, bearer auth with the GBRAIN_PROXY_TOKEN env var (always write it as "authorization: Bearer $GBRAIN_PROXY_TOKEN", never print or inline the value). Calls: GET /gbrain/person/<person id>?actor=<your name>&event_id=<event id> (person card: relationship, facts, open loops, last seen); POST /gbrain/query with JSON {"q": ..., "actor": "<your name>", "event_id": "<event id>"} (hybrid search, returns slug, title, snippet); GET /gbrain/page/<slug>?actor=<your name>&event_id=<event id> (one page). Use curl -sS -m 20 and save each response as a .json file in your event dir. If a call fails (unreachable, 401, 503), write the status into the file and continue from the world event alone. Resolve who is asking and what we already know. Use the execute tool (shell) for all file work. 1) mkdir -p $HOME/world/<event id> $HOME/world/signals && cd $HOME/world/<event id>. You MUST read GBrain first: curl the person card for <the first id in the event's people that is not stephen> into gbrain-person.json, then POST /gbrain/query for prior feedback and requests from this person and project (q like "<name> <product> feedback requests") into gbrain-prior.json. 2) Append one line (date, requester, product, feature, request) to $HOME/world/signals/<product>-requests.log and count distinct requesters. 3) Write context.md in $HOME/world/<event id>/ with the person card (name, role and company, relationship, open loops from GBrain), the prior signal count, prior related requests by GBrain slug, and a final 'Summary:' line of at most 40 words for the coding agent. 4) Send that Summary line to the Builder worker and to the root with a swarm send. 5) Verify with: test -s $HOME/world/<event id>/context.md && grep -qi 'signal' $HOME/world/<event id>/context.md && echo CONTEXT_OK. Report to the root.

workers.name: Product
workers.brief: GBrain (the owner's declarative memory) is readable through the owner's WORLD service at http://host.docker.internal:8787/gbrain, read-only, bearer auth with the GBRAIN_PROXY_TOKEN env var (always write it as "authorization: Bearer $GBRAIN_PROXY_TOKEN", never print or inline the value). Calls: GET /gbrain/person/<person id>?actor=<your name>&event_id=<event id> (person card: relationship, facts, open loops, last seen); POST /gbrain/query with JSON {"q": ..., "actor": "<your name>", "event_id": "<event id>"} (hybrid search, returns slug, title, snippet); GET /gbrain/page/<slug>?actor=<your name>&event_id=<event id> (one page). Use curl -sS -m 20 and save each response as a .json file in your event dir. If a call fails (unreachable, 401, 503), write the status into the file and continue from the world event alone. Spec the requested change so a coding agent can build it. Use the execute tool (shell) for all file work. 1) mkdir -p $HOME/world/<event id> && cd $HOME/world/<event id>. Before speccing, query GBrain for similar past requests (q like "<product> <feature> requests") into gbrain-similar.json and for existing procedures (q like "procedures <feature>", look for procedures/* slugs) into gbrain-procedures.json; read the top procedures/* page if there is one. 2) Write spec.md there with: title, user story, acceptance criteria (a checklist of at least three testable items), files likely touched, out of scope, and 'Prior art:' with the GBrain slugs (similar requests, procedure) you used. 3) Also write spec.json there: {"title": ..., "summary": ..., "acceptance_criteria": [...], "files_likely_touched": [...], "prior_art": [slugs]}. 4) Verify with: test -s $HOME/world/<event id>/spec.md && grep -qi 'acceptance' $HOME/world/<event id>/spec.md && python3 -m json.tool $HOME/world/<event id>/spec.json >/dev/null && echo SPEC_OK. Send the spec.json content to the root and to the Builder worker with a swarm send.

workers.name: Builder
workers.brief: Dispatch the coding job to the owner's WORLD builder, which runs Claude Code as this swarm's hands (target repo qtzx06/opal, Discord bot). The spec is the world event payload itself; do not wait for Product. Use the execute tool (shell) for all file work. 1) Check swarm messages (GET /v1/swarm?read=1) for the Context worker's Summary line, waiting at most 60 seconds in total; if it has not arrived, use the gbrain_context block in the event, or an empty string. 2) mkdir -p $HOME/world/<event id> and write dispatch.json there: {"event_id": <the world event id>, "person_id": <the first id in the event's people that is not stephen>, "spec": <the event payload object, verbatim, plus one extra key "context": the Context summary string>}. 3) POST it with: cd $HOME/world/<event id> && curl -sS -m 20 -o dispatch-response.json -w '%{http_code}' -H 'content-type: application/json' --data @dispatch.json http://host.docker.internal:8787/builder/dispatch > dispatch-status.txt || echo "unreachable: curl exit $?" > dispatch-status.txt. The builder dedupes by event_id, so never post twice. 4) Verify with: test -s $HOME/world/<event id>/dispatch.json && test -s $HOME/world/<event id>/dispatch-status.txt && echo DISPATCH_OK. Report the HTTP status and any job id, status, or URL from dispatch-response.json to the root.

commitment.detected.action: The owner made a commitment in person. Record it, find the asset it refers to if one exists, and reply with a one line reminder. Do not contact the recipient.
